title: Powertools for AWS Lambda: idempotent handlers
intro: Excerpts from the idempotency utility of Powertools for AWS Lambda (TypeScript). It makes a Lambda handler, or any function, safe to retry: the first call with a given payload runs and its result is stored; later calls with the same payload get the stored result instead of running again. The real persistence stores (DynamoDB, Redis) are not included; stubs.ts describes what they guarantee. Start with handle() in IdempotencyHandler.ts, then persistence/BasePersistenceLayer.ts.

questions.text: Walk through what happens on the first call of an idempotent function, and then on a second call with the same payload after the first has completed.
How is the idempotency key built from the incoming event? What do eventKeyJmesPath and the key prefix contribute?
What do the two timestamps on an IdempotencyRecord mean, and what units is each one in?
Could a request that the caller retries ever be processed twice even though idempotency is enabled? Under what conditions? Point to the lines with a code comment if you can.
Why does the handler delete the in-progress record when the wrapped function throws, instead of saving the failure?
Why are records with status INPROGRESS never put in the local cache?
How would you test that the same logical request always maps to the same idempotency key?
Two invocations with the same key arrive at the same time. What does the second one get today, and what would you change to give callers a better outcome?
